claim: Retrieval practice beats restudy on delayed tests but loses on immediate tests (crossover). The gain is large (d about 0.8-1.2 at 2 days to 1 week) and held across materials and samples. Boundary: two 2026 online (Prolific) experiments found no benefit (N=67 and N=129, heavy attrition), so the effect can fail in noisy, low-engagement samples.
agent_test: Compare an agent that rereads its notes vs one that must regenerate the answer from memory before reading, at equal tokens, on a delayed (many turns later) fact test.
audit_note: Roediger & Karpicke 2006 Exp 1: restudy better at 5 min (81 vs 75%), testing better at 2 days (d=0.95) and 1 week (d=0.83); Sigayret et al. 2026: N=67 and N=129 analysed with heavy attrition, no significant delayed-test difference (not 'no benefit'; Exp 2 was numerically higher for testing); upper d of 1.2 not checked.

claim: Retrieval practice engages hippocampus and medial PFC more than restudy at encoding, and the engagement predicts later memory.
agent_test: Not testable on an LLM; analogue is whether retrieval-style rereading changes which stored notes are used later.
audit_note: Wing, Marsh & Cabeza 2013: initial testing that led to later success engaged anterior hippocampus and medial PFC versus restudy; Wiklund-Hornqvist 2021 shows hippocampal activity rising with successful retrievals but measured at the delayed test and without a restudy contrast, so it supports the claim only indirectly; single fMRI contrast study base.

claim: The strong fast-consolidation neural prediction (hippocampus falls and mPFC rises within one session of retrieval) is only partly supported. The mPFC rise held in one test; the hippocampal fall appeared only across days; a rehearsal-recall study found a within-session shift. Ferreira 2018 was published (NeuroImage 2019): the mPFC rise and gist gains grew across two days, not within the session. A 2026 Current Biology fMRI study also found mPFC abstraction emerging across days.
agent_test: None needed; background for how much weight to give the consolidation framing.

claim: Schema-congruent material gains a memory advantage after a consolidation delay (not at once) in humans, and new schema-fitting items become hippocampus-independent quickly in rats.
agent_test: Store new facts linked to an existing structure vs as isolated notes; measure recall after a long gap at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: The retrieval benefit depends on meaning or prior knowledge (meaningless squiggles show no testing benefit; meaningful objects do after delay), but it does not depend on how well items were first studied. Related-pair testing benefit is 26% smaller than unrelated in one controlled 24 h experiment (N=231), but Rowland 2014 found g 0.66 vs 0.67 and other studies are mixed.
agent_test: Test retrieval-first rereading on meaningful vs arbitrary content (random IDs vs domain facts).

claim: Sleep right after learning helps restudied items more than retrieval-practised items over 12 h, which shrinks the testing effect. The pattern vanishes at 24 h and 7 days and when corrective feedback is given.
agent_test: No sleep in LLMs; closest analogue is an offline consolidation pass (see the sleep-time compute claim).
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: A CLS-based model says sleep flips retrieval-practice effects only for far, unrelated untested pairmates; retrieval always helps close pairmates and hurts far ones.
agent_test: Check retrieval-induced forgetting in an agent: after retrieving fact A, is related fact B recalled worse or better?

claim: Retrieval practice of a new association can reduce intrusions of an old competing association, with or without suppressing the old one. Evidence is mixed across paradigms.
agent_test: Update test: A-B then A-C; compare retrieving the new vs rereading the new, and count old-answer intrusions.

claim: Reminder-then-new-learning reconsolidation is contested. The Hupbach 2007 intrusion effect replicated at 3 days and meta-analysed (d about 1.03), but the motor-sequence and recognition versions failed to replicate, and a reminder test can immunise memory against interference.
agent_test: Do not build on reconsolidation; test only whether a reminder before new info raises intrusions in a prompted agent.

claim: The testing effect is not explained by consolidation alone. Rival accounts (mediators, retrieval effort, dual memory with independent traces) fit the data, and the dual-memory model predicts effect size with no consolidation parameter.
agent_test: None; informs how to read agent results (a gain does not prove consolidation).

claim: In one EEG study (N=30) retrieval training, but not sleep, merged similar-object representations.
agent_test: Check whether retrieval-style practice makes an agent confuse similar items (lure discrimination).

claim: No controlled LLM study replicating the human testing effect, retrieval-induced forgetting or reconsolidation was found. The searches were limited (arXiv only, rate limited).
agent_test: Run the first one: retrieval-before-reread vs reread on a delayed fact benchmark in a fixed-token agent.

claim: Training weights on questions before or alongside documents, or on self-generated study material (QA, paraphrases, implications), makes facts far easier to retrieve than reading documents alone. This is the closest LLM analogue of retrieval practice.
agent_test: Prompt-level only: have the agent write its own questions about new notes before storing them; compare later recall at equal tokens.
audit_note: Jiang et al. (pre-instruction-tuning on QA before documents, ~17.8% QA accuracy gain on Llama-2), Allen-Zhu & Li (augmentation needed for extractability) and Lin et al. (self-generated study material, +313% relative on SimpleQA) support the facts-easier-to-retrieve claim; 'closest LLM analogue of retrieval practice' is an interpretation, not a finding.

claim: Offline pre-computation over stored context (sleep-time compute) cuts test-time compute about 5x at equal accuracy when queries are predictable from context.
agent_test: Compare answering from raw notes vs notes plus an offline digest, on predictable and unpredictable query sets.

claim: Rewriting memories into short notes loses information later readers need: aspect (progressive becomes simple present), hedges (become confident facts) and dates (dropped in gist compression).
agent_test: Store both the gist note and the user's original wording; compare error rates in later decisions at equal tokens.
audit_note: Panthi et al. (aspect flattening in 210 of 381 pairs, all 11 models), Kwon (hedged remarks stored as confident assertions in mem0/LangMem; single-author preprint) and Kyrkewood (gist prompt discards dates: 3.05% temporal preservation, recoverable to 62.39% with a one-sentence prompt change) support it; losses are prompt-dependent, not inevitable.

claim: Agent loops that write reflections, verified skills or linked notes back into memory beat raw-trace memory in the authors' own ablations.
agent_test: Ablation: raw-trace memory vs reflection note vs linked note on a repeated-task set at equal tokens.
audit_note: Park (ablating reflection lowers believability), Reflexion (+8% absolute over episodic-memory-only), A-MEM (w/o LG&ME far below full) and Voyager (ablating skill library hurts) all report own ablations; comparators differ (Voyager ablates having a skill library, not raw-trace memory) and all are authors' own self-reported results.

claim: Write-time linking of new items into an existing graph (HippoRAG, A-MEM) improves multi-hop retrieval, the engineering parallel of schema integration.
agent_test: Link-on-write vs append-only store, scored on multi-hop questions.
audit_note: HippoRAG reports gains of about 3-20 points over RAG on MuSiQue/2WikiMultiHopQA from an index-time knowledge graph; A-MEM ablation shows link generation lifts multi-hop F1 (w/o LG&ME 9.65 vs 27.02); HippoRAG builds the graph over a corpus rather than strictly linking each new item into a pre-existing graph, and 'schema integration' parallel is interpretive.

claim: A recall-strength rule (recalled items last longer) was implemented in MemoryBank but never ablated.
agent_test: Add a strength-on-recall rule to the agent store; compare with flat retention.

claim: LLM-written retrieval-practice quizzes raised next-week student quiz accuracy (89% vs 73%) in a non-randomised quasi-experiment.
agent_test: Weak design; replicate with random assignment if the topic is pursued.

claim: A learned forget-and-merge gate over the KV cache restores newest-value retrieval under proactive interference in a tiny synthetic setting, and collapses at deep stale depth.
agent_test: Prompt-level version: mark superseded entries and test newest-value recall with growing update depth.

claim: Direct published tests of the Antony 2017 hippocampus-falls prediction remain limited to Ferreira 2019 (NeuroImage), which supports a retrieval-driven mPFC gain and generalisation but only across days, with episode detail also strengthened.
agent_test: None needed.

claim: The testing-effect gain is smaller for strongly related material (about 26% smaller, N=231, one lab), yet the Rowland 2014 meta-analysis found no difference (g 0.66 related vs 0.67 unrelated). Evidence on schema-poor vs schema-rich material is mixed.
agent_test: Test retrieve-first on isolated vs well-linked facts at equal tokens.

claim: Consolidation by rewriting pulls recalled content toward prior knowledge in an LLM (Mistral 7B, Bartlett-style story), matching human distortion over time. A plausible mechanism for tense and hedge flattening in note stores, but a model result, not an agent test.
agent_test: Keep raw wording beside the summary; compare error rates.

claim: Fast consolidation into schemas needs a schema built first (Tse 2007 rats, many trials); effect sizes could not be read in full here.
agent_test: None; background.

claim: No LLM or agent study was found testing retrieval-before-reread, question-first study, retrieval-induced forgetting, or verbatim-kept notes. Weak negative: search tools were rate-limited.
agent_test: Run the four tests ourselves.

claim: A two-speed LLM memory (fast per-episode adapters, slow replay fine-tuning) is being tried at 1,000-episode scale in a 2026 preprint; weight-level, not usable by a prompt-only scaffold.
agent_test: None for the scaffold.
